stages.name: Outside the war
stages.desc: Kingdoms, leagues and islands that kept out of the two great alliances

stages.name: Athens and its allies
stages.desc: Athens, its tribute-paying Aegean empire and its allied states

stages.name: Sparta and its allies
stages.desc: Sparta, Corinth, Thebes and the Peloponnesian League

stages.name: In revolt from Athens
stages.desc: Former subjects of Athens that broke away, often with Spartan help

stages.name: Invaded or occupied
stages.desc: An enemy army on the land or a garrison inside its borders

states.name: West Macedonia
timeline: The kingdom of Macedon, whose king changes sides as it suits him
King Perdiccas joins Brasidas against Athens
Perdiccas quarrels with Brasidas and makes terms with Athens

states.name: Epirus
timeline: The tribal kingdoms of Epirus, outside the Greek alliances

states.name: Centre Macedonia
timeline: Potidaea and the Chalcidian towns pay tribute to Athens
Athens founds Amphipolis on the river Strymon
Potidaea revolts; Athens besieges it, with Socrates and Alcibiades in the ranks
Starving Potidaea surrenders
Brasidas takes Amphipolis and the Chalcidian towns go over to him
Athens fails to retake Amphipolis; Socrates serves in the campaign
Sparta dominates the north

states.name: East Macedonia and Thrace
timeline: Thasos and the Thracian coast pay tribute to Athens
Thasos overthrows its democracy and revolts
Thrasybulus brings Thasos back to the Athenian side
After Athens falls, Spartan governors take over

states.name: Mount Athos
timeline: Small tribute-paying towns of the Athos peninsula
Most towns of the peninsula go over to Brasidas
Sparta dominates the north

states.name: Thessalia
timeline: Thessalian lords, nominal allies of Athens, keep out of most of the fighting
The Spartan Brasidas marches through Thessaly to the north

states.name: Central Greece
timeline: Boeotia under Athenian control since the victory at Oenophyta
Defeat at Coronea: Boeotia breaks free; Alcibiades' father is among the dead
The Boeotians rout the Athenians at Delium
Euboea, Athens' granary, revolts

states.name: Attica
timeline: Athens under Pericles, capital of an empire of some two hundred Aegean cities
Work begins on the Parthenon
Spartan armies invade Attica; the country people crowd inside the Long Walls
Plague strikes the overcrowded city
With Spartan prisoners from Pylos held hostage, the invasions stop
The herms are mutilated; Alcibiades is accused of mocking the Mysteries
On Alcibiades' advice, the Spartans fortify Decelea and hold the countryside all year
Alcibiades returns in triumph and leads the Eleusis procession under armed guard
Athens surrenders; under Spartan protection, the Thirty rule the city

states.name: Peloponnese
timeline: Sparta, Corinth and the Peloponnesian League; Argos stays neutral
Alcibiades draws Argos and Mantinea into an alliance with Athens
Sparta wins the battle of Mantinea and restores its control
Alcibiades, a fugitive, advises the Spartans against his own city

states.name: West Greece
timeline: Elis, keeper of Olympia, and the Achaean cities follow Sparta; Athens holds Naupactus
Elis joins Alcibiades' alliance and bars the Spartans from the Olympic Games
The alliance breaks up after Mantinea; Elis keeps aloof from both sides
Alcibiades' seven chariots race at Olympia
With Athens defeated, Sparta dominates the whole of Greece

states.name: Crete
timeline: The cities of Crete stay outside the war

states.name: South Aegean
timeline: The Cyclades and Rhodes, tribute-paying members of Athens' league
Athens conquers neutral Melos, kills its men and enslaves its women and children
Rhodes revolts and goes over to Sparta
After Aegospotami, Lysander takes over the islands

states.name: North Aegean
timeline: Lesbos, Chios and Samos, Athens' strongest allies, with fleets of their own
Samos revolts; Pericles besieges it for nine months
Samos surrenders and loses its fleet
Mytilene leads Lesbos in revolt
Mytilene surrenders; Athens votes to kill its men, then relents
Chios and Lesbos revolt; Alcibiades sails with the Spartan ships
Samos becomes the Athenian fleet's base; the sailors recall Alcibiades
After Aegospotami, the islands go over to Lysander; only Samos holds out
Samos too surrenders

states.name: Ionian Islands
timeline: Corcyra, a great naval power, keeps out of the alliances
Corcyra makes a defensive alliance with Athens
Civil war tears Corcyra apart
The great armada for Sicily gathers at Corcyra
With Athens defeated, Corcyra stands alone

events.title: Alcibiades is born
events.text: Alcibiades, son of Cleinias, is born into one of Athens' great families, about this year.

events.title: Battle of Coronea
events.text: His father dies fighting the Boeotians; the boy becomes the ward of his kinsman Pericles.

events.title: The Parthenon begun
events.text: Pericles' building programme begins on the Acropolis, paid for partly by the allies' tribute.

events.title: Samos revolts
events.text: Pericles crushes the revolt of Samos after a nine-month siege.

events.title: Corcyra joins Athens
events.text: Athens allies with Corcyra against Corinth, one of the sparks of the great war.

events.title: Siege of Potidaea
events.text: Socrates saves the wounded Alcibiades, then lets him take the prize for valour, Plato later writes.

events.title: War begins
events.text: The Spartan king Archidamus invades Attica: the Peloponnesian War has begun.

events.title: Plague in Athens
events.text: Plague kills perhaps a quarter of the crowded city's people.

events.title: Pericles dies
events.text: Alcibiades' guardian dies of the plague.

events.title: Plato is born
events.text: Plato is born in Athens or Aegina about this year, some twenty years after Alcibiades.

events.title: Mytilene subdued
events.text: Athens votes to kill every man of rebel Mytilene, then sends a second ship to cancel the order.

events.title: Pylos and Sphacteria
events.text: Athens captures 292 Spartans on Sphacteria, a shock to all of Greece.

events.title: Battle of Delium
events.text: In the Athenian rout, Alcibiades on horseback stays beside Socrates on foot.

events.title: Amphipolis falls
events.text: The Spartan Brasidas takes Athens' northern colony of Amphipolis.

events.title: Battle of Amphipolis
events.text: Brasidas and the Athenian leader Cleon are both killed, opening the way to peace.

events.title: Peace of Nicias
events.text: Athens and Sparta make a fifty-year peace; it lasts barely seven.

events.title: Alliance with Argos
events.text: Alcibiades, now a general, builds an alliance of Athens, Argos, Mantinea and Elis.

events.title: Battle of Mantinea
events.text: Sparta defeats the alliance in the largest land battle of the war.

events.title: Seven chariots
events.text: Alcibiades enters seven chariots at Olympia and takes first, second and fourth places.

events.title: Agathon's victory
events.text: The poet Agathon wins the tragedy prize: the night of Plato's Symposium.

events.title: Melos destroyed
events.text: Athens kills the men of neutral Melos and enslaves the women and children.

events.title: The herms mutilated
events.text: Statues of Hermes across Athens are smashed in one night; Alcibiades is accused of sacrilege.

events.title: The fleet sails
events.text: More than a hundred warships leave for Sicily under Nicias, Lamachus and Alcibiades.

events.title: Escape at Thurii
events.text: Recalled to stand trial, Alcibiades slips away; Athens condemns him to death.

events.title: Advice to Sparta
events.text: Alcibiades tells the Spartans to send a general to Syracuse and to fortify Decelea.

events.title: Siege of Syracuse
events.text: The Spartan Gylippus reaches Syracuse and turns the siege against the Athenians.

events.title: Decelea fortified
events.text: A Spartan garrison in Attica cuts Athens off from its fields and silver mines.

events.title: Disaster in Sicily
events.text: The Athenian army is destroyed; thousands die in the stone quarries of Syracuse.

events.title: Chios revolts
events.text: Alcibiades sails with a Spartan squadron and brings Chios over to Sparta.

events.title: With Tissaphernes
events.text: Alcibiades goes over to the Persian governor at Sardis, and advises him to let the Greeks wear each other out.

events.title: Recalled at Samos
events.text: The Athenian fleet at Samos elects Alcibiades its general.

events.title: The Four Hundred
events.text: Oligarchs overthrow the democracy in Athens for four months.

events.title: Victory at Cyzicus
events.text: Alcibiades and his colleagues destroy the Spartan fleet in the Sea of Marmara.

events.title: Byzantium retaken
events.text: Alcibiades wins back Byzantium and the grain route from the Black Sea.

events.title: Return to Athens
events.text: After eight years in exile, Alcibiades sails into Piraeus to cheering crowds.

events.title: Procession to Eleusis
events.text: He escorts the sacred procession to Eleusis by land under armed guard.

events.title: Defeat at Notium
events.text: His deputy fights against orders and loses; Alcibiades is not re-elected.

events.title: Retreat to Thrace
events.text: Alcibiades withdraws to his private forts on the Gallipoli peninsula.

events.title: Warning at Aegospotami
events.text: He rides into the Athenian camp to warn the generals; days later the fleet is destroyed.

events.title: Athens surrenders
events.text: The Long Walls are pulled down; Sparta's Lysander sets up the Thirty, led by Plato's kinsman Critias.

events.title: Death in Phrygia
events.text: In a Phrygian village, Persian killers set fire to his house and shoot him as he rushes out.

chartNote: Share of the area of today's Greece, by the side taken by the ancient cities in each modern region. Regions are today's boundaries and each held several cities with different loyalties; the map shows the dominant side, a simplification of a war in which allegiances changed constantly.
